meta.title: Halvorsen Motors SOC investigation console
meta.source: Generated by build_page_kit.py from the hm-* dashboards in folder halvorsen-soc. Queries, card text and links match the dashboards.
meta.replay: A scripted intrusion replays at the top of every UTC hour over about 30 minutes. Victim rotates jakub.kowalski, aisha.nguyen, carlos.ortega by hour.
query_notes: LogQL. $__range is the selected range as a duration, $__interval the step. Variables appear as $name or ${name}.
instant queries return a vector: one row per label set, value in the last element.
Severity label is detected_level, not severity_text.
Keep each query under 500 series; the expressions here already are.

link_params.row.<col>: another column of the same row

workflows.title: 00 Start here: triage queue
workflows.description: Work leads top to bottom. Red means there is something to work. Click the blue name to open its workflow.
intro:
## Start here
1. Work the leads **top to bottom**. They are ordered by how often they turn out to be the start of an intrusion.
2. A **red number** means the lead has something to work. Green means skip it.
3. In the lead's table, **click the blue value**. It opens the workflow for that lead with the user, host or asset filled in.
4. Each workflow ends with a **Decide** step that tells you whether to escalate and which workflow comes next. Add every user, host and IP you touch to the **case timeline**.

_Synthetic data. A scripted intrusion replays at the top of every UTC hour over about 30 minutes._

leads.title: Suspicious sign-in

evidence.title: Users with 5+ denied MFA pushes
evidence.expr: count(sum by (user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | event_type="user.mfa.push" | outcome="FAILURE" [$__range])) >= 5)

evidence.title: Denied MFA pushes by user (click the user)
evidence.expr: sum by (user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | event_type="user.mfa.push" | outcome="FAILURE" [$__range])) >= 5

leads.why: Repeated MFA prompts the user did not start (MFA fatigue) are how a sprayed password becomes a working session.

leads.title: Endpoint detection that was not blocked

evidence.title: Hosts with allowed high/critical detections
evidence.expr: count(sum by (host) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | event_type="Detection" | severity=~"high|critical" | action="allowed" [$__range])))

evidence.title: Allowed high/critical detections (click the host)
evidence.expr: topk(20, sum by (host, user, detection_name) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | event_type="Detection" | severity=~"high|critical" | action="allowed" [$__range])))

leads.why: High and critical EDR detections where the action was *allowed* ran to completion. Someone has to look.

leads.title: Credential theft and lateral movement

evidence.title: Hosts requesting RC4 service tickets
evidence.expr: count(sum by (src_host) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | event_id="4769" | ticket_encryption="0x17" [$__range])))

evidence.title: RC4 service tickets by source host (click the host)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | event_id="4769" | ticket_encryption="0x17" [$__range]))

leads.why: RC4 Kerberos service tickets (0x17). The fleet is AES-only, so RC4 requests mean someone is Kerberoasting service accounts.
leads.work_in: WF3 Lateral movement and privilege escalation

leads.title: Large upload to file sharing

evidence.title: Users over 100 MB
evidence.expr: count(sum by (user) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])) > 100000000)

evidence.title: Uploads to file sharing over 100 MB (click the user)
evidence.expr: sum by (user, host, url_domain) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])) > 100000000

leads.why: Over 100 MB to a personal file-sharing site from a corporate host. Vehicle program data is the crown jewel here.

leads.title: Unticketed change on the plant floor

evidence.title: Unticketed controller changes
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | change_ticket="" | event_type=~"program_download|controller_mode_change|write_request" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Unticketed controller changes by asset (click the asset)
evidence.expr: sum by (site, asset, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | change_ticket="" | event_type=~"program_download|controller_mode_change|write_request" [$__range]))

leads.why: A program download, mode change or setpoint write with no change ticket. This can stop a line or hurt someone.

leads.title: Vehicle API key abuse

evidence.title: Keys with over 150 404s
evidence.expr: count(sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | status=404 [$__range])) > 150)

evidence.title: 404s by API key, all keys (click the key)
evidence.expr: sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | status=404 [$__range]))

leads.why: Hundreds of 404s on one key means someone is guessing VINs. A hit returns a customer's car location.

workflows.title: WF1 Suspicious sign-in
workflows.description: Decide whether a user's account is compromised. MFA fatigue, password spray, impossible travel.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead A on the triage queue, or a user reports MFA prompts they did not start.  
**You need:** the user name (top of the page).  
**Goal:** decide whether this account is compromised. About 5 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Denied pushes
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | event_type="user.mfa.push" | outcome="FAILURE" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Approved pushes
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | event_type="user.mfa.push" | outcome="SUCCESS" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Push outcomes
evidence.expr: sum by (outcome) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | event_type="user.mfa.push" [$__interval]))

evidence.title: Push log, oldest first
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | event_type="user.mfa.push" | line_format "{{.outcome}} {{.reason}}  from {{.src_ip}} {{.src_country}} {{.src_city}}  app={{.app}}" | keep service_name

card.look: denied pushes over time, then the push log in order.
card.bad: 3 or more denied or timed-out pushes within about 10 minutes, followed by a SUCCESS.
card.if_bad: note the source IP of the success and go to Step 2.
card.if_clean: one or two failures then a success from the usual device is a fumble. Still do Step 3.

steps.title: Where did the sign-in come from?

evidence.title: Sign-in and VPN sources for this user
evidence.expr: topk(25, sum by (service_name, src_ip, src_country, outcome, user_agent) (count_over_time({service_name=~"secdemo-idp|secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" [$__range])))

card.look: every source the user signed in from, with country and client.
card.bad: a country the user does not work in, a hosting or residential IP nobody else uses, or a script client (`python-requests`, `curl`).
card.if_bad: this is the attacker's address. Copy it into the case timeline and go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: US or MX home and office addresses with a normal browser are expected.

evidence.title: High-risk attempts against this user
evidence.expr: sum by (src_ip, src_country, outcome, reason, user_agent) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user="$user" | risk_level="HIGH" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Users hit by script-client sign-ins
evidence.expr: count(sum by (user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-idp"} | json | user_agent=~"python.*|curl.*" [$__range])))
evidence.help: Breadth of the spray. Every one of these users needs a password check, not just this one.

card.look: high-risk sign-in attempts against this user, and how many other users the same spray hit.
card.bad: a SUCCESS or `PASSWORD_OK_MFA_REQUIRED` from a spray address. The password is compromised even if MFA held.
card.if_bad: the password must be reset regardless of anything else. Continue to Step 4.
card.if_clean: no high-risk attempts against this user. The sign-in may still be bad if Step 1 or 2 was red.

steps.title: Can the user be in two places?

evidence.title: Badge and VPN, oldest first
evidence.expr: {service_name=~"secdemo-badge|secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" | line_format "{{.service_name}}  {{or .door .event}}  {{.site}}  {{.src_country}} {{.src_ip}}  hip={{.hip_compliant}}" | keep service_name

card.look: badge reads and VPN connections for this user, in time order.
card.bad: a badge read at a US site within an hour of a VPN connect from abroad, or `hip_compliant=false` (device failed the posture check).
card.if_bad: the remote session is not the user. Treat as compromised. Go to Step 5.
card.if_clean: badge and VPN tell one consistent story.

evidence.title: Hosts this user was active on (click to open WF2)
evidence.expr: topk(10, sum by (host) (count_over_time({service_name=~"secdemo-edr|secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | host!="" [$__range])))

evidence.title: Times added to a group
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | target_user="$user" | event_id=~"4728|4732|4756" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Uploaded to file sharing
evidence.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range]))

card.look: the hosts this user was active on, privilege changes made to the account, and uploads.
card.bad: a host with EDR detections, the user added to a group, or large uploads.
card.if_bad: click the host to open WF2. If uploads are large, open WF4 from the Decide step.
card.if_clean: ordinary activity on the user's own workstation.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Compromised** if Step 1 or Step 3 was red **and** Step 2 or Step 4 was red.

**If compromised, do these now:**
1. Revoke all IdP sessions and refresh tokens for the user.
2. Reset the password and force MFA re-enrolment.
3. Block the source IP from Step 2 at the IdP and VPN.
4. Open a case and add the user, IP and hosts to it.

**Then go to:**
- WF2 for each host in Step 5 (click it in the table)
- [[WF4 Data exfiltration]] if Step 5 showed uploads
- [[Case timeline]]

**Not compromised:** close the lead with a note on which step cleared it.

rule.close_if_false: Not compromised. Close the lead with the step that cleared it.

workflows.title: WF2 Compromised endpoint
workflows.description: Scope one host: what ran, how it got in, whether it persists, whether it calls out, whether it spread.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead B, or WF1 Step 5 pointed at a host.  
**You need:** the host name, and the user if you have it.  
**Goal:** decide whether to contain the host and find where the attacker went next. About 10 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Detections on this host
evidence.expr: sum by (severity, detection_name, technique_id, action, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | event_type="Detection" [$__range]))

card.look: every detection on the host, worst first.
card.bad: high or critical with action `allowed`, or several tactics in a row (Execution, Persistence, Discovery, Credential Access).
card.if_bad: go to Step 2 to see how it started.
card.if_clean: a single low or medium detection that was blocked or quarantined. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Suspicious process chain on this host
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | event_type="Detection" | line_format "{{.parent_process}} -> {{.process}}   [{{.technique_id}}]  {{.cmdline}}" | keep service_name

card.look: the process chain, oldest first.
card.bad: an Office app (`excel.exe`, `winword.exe`, `outlook.exe`) starting `powershell`, `cmd`, `rundll32` or `mshta`; `-enc` or `-w hidden` on the command line.
card.if_bad: Office as the parent means a malicious attachment. Go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: the chain starts from explorer or a known updater.

steps.title: Did it come in by email?

evidence.title: Mail to this user from new domains
evidence.expr: sum by (sender_domain, subject, attachment, verdict, domain_age_days) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-email"} | json | recipient=~"$user@.*" | domain_age_days < 30 [$__range]))

evidence.title: Everyone who got mail from new domains (click to open WF1)
evidence.expr: topk(40, sum by (recipient_user, sender_domain, verdict) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-email"} | json | domain_age_days < 30 | label_format recipient_user=`{{ regexReplaceAll "@.*" .recipient "" }}` [$__range])))

card.look: mail the user received from domains younger than 30 days, then everyone else who got the same mail.
card.bad: a delivered message from a new lookalike domain with a macro attachment (`.xlsm`, `.docm`) shortly before Step 2.
card.if_bad: every other delivered recipient is a potential second victim. Click each one to open WF1.
card.if_clean: nothing from a new domain. The entry point was something else (web, USB, VPN). Keep going.

evidence.title: Persistence on this host
evidence.expr: sum by (detection_name, technique_id, process, cmdline) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | technique_id=~"T1053.*|T1543.*|T1547.*" [$__range]))

card.look: scheduled tasks, services and run keys created on the host.
card.bad: `schtasks /create`, a new service or a run key pointing at a user-writable path (AppData, Temp, ProgramData).
card.if_bad: note the task name and binary for the eradication list.
card.if_clean: no persistence found. Containment may be enough.

steps.title: Is it talking to command and control?

evidence.title: Small outbound sessions per destination (beacons are flat lines)
evidence.expr: topk(5, sum by (dst_domain) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | src_host="$host" | dst_zone="internet" | bytes < 2000 [5m])))

evidence.title: New domains this host resolved
evidence.expr: sum by (query, domain_age_days, category) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-dns"} | json | host="$host" | domain_age_days < 30 [$__range]))

card.look: small, regular outbound connections per destination, and new domains the host resolved.
card.bad: one destination every minute with almost identical size (a flat line), or a domain under 30 days old.
card.if_bad: block the domain and IP at the firewall and DNS. Add them to the case.
card.if_clean: outbound traffic is bursty and goes to known SaaS.

evidence.title: RC4 service tickets requested
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id="4769" | ticket_encryption="0x17" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Explicit-credential logons to other hosts
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id="4648" | target_user!~"adm-.*" [$__range]))
evidence.help: 4648 with a different account. Personal adm- accounts via runas are excluded.

evidence.title: RDP or SMB sessions out
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | src_host="$host" | dst_port=~"3389|445|5985" | action="allow" [$__range]))

card.look: three counters for movement off this host.
card.bad: any red counter.
card.if_bad: open [[WF3 Lateral movement from this host]].
card.if_clean: all green. The attacker probably stayed on this host.

links.label: WF3 Lateral movement from this host

evidence.title: Already contained?
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | event_type="Containment" [$__range]))
evidence.help: Orange 0 = not contained yet. Green = an analyst already contained it.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Contain the host** if Step 1 had an allowed high/critical detection **and** Step 2 or Step 5 was bad.

**Do these now:**
1. Network-contain the host in EDR. Do not power it off; memory is evidence.
2. Block the C2 domain and IP from Step 5.
3. Purge the lure email from every mailbox in Step 3.
4. Add the persistence items from Step 4 to the eradication list.

**Then go to:**
- [[WF3 Lateral movement from this host]] if any Step 6 counter was red
- [[WF1 for the user]] to check the account
- [[WF4 Data exfiltration]]
- [[Case timeline for the host]]

links.label: WF3 Lateral movement from this host

also.say: Movement off this host. Run WF3 from here.

rule.close_if_false: No containment needed. Close the lead.

workflows.title: WF3 Lateral movement and privilege escalation
workflows.description: Follow the attacker host by host. Run once per hop.
intro:
**Use when:** WF2 Step 6 was red, or Lead C.  
**You need:** the host you are on now.  
**Goal:** build the full list of hosts and accounts the attacker used. That list is your containment scope.

> **How to follow the trail:** write the current host on your case notes. In **Step 4**, click a destination host. The page reloads with that host as the current hop. Repeat until Step 4 is empty. Every host you wrote down gets contained.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Credential theft detections
evidence.expr: sum by (detection_name, technique_id, process, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-edr"} | json | host="$host" | tactic="Credential Access" | action="allowed" [$__range]))

evidence.title: RC4 tickets requested from this host (service accounts at risk)
evidence.expr: sum by (spn, user) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id="4769" | ticket_encryption="0x17" [$__range]))

card.look: credential-access detections on this host and Kerberos tickets it requested with RC4.
card.bad: LSASS access, `sekurlsa`, `procdump lsass`, or RC4 tickets for many service accounts in a few seconds.
card.if_bad: every account that logged on to this host and every listed service account is burned. Add them to the reset list.
card.if_clean: no credential theft here. The attacker may be reusing credentials stolen elsewhere.

steps.title: Which accounts were used from here?

evidence.title: Accounts used from this host
evidence.expr: sum by (event_id, user, target_user, logon_type, dst_host) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id=~"4624|4648" [$__range]))
evidence.help: logon_type 3 = network, 10 = RDP. 4648 = explicit credentials (runas, PsExec).

card.look: logons from this host to anywhere, and logons that switched to a different account.
card.bad: a service account (`svc_*`) or admin account used from a workstation, or a 4648 where `target_user` is not the person at the keyboard.
card.if_bad: add each account to the reset list. Service accounts also need their SPN password rotated.
card.if_clean: only the host's own user, logging on to the usual servers.

evidence.title: Privilege changes from this host
evidence.expr: sum by (event_id, event_name, user, target_user, group, service, dst_host) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id=~"4672|4728|4732|4756|7045" [$__range]))

card.look: privileged logons, group additions and services installed from this host.
card.bad: an account added to an admin or OT engineering group, `SeDebugPrivilege` on a service account, or a service like `PSEXESVC` installed on another machine.
card.if_bad: undo the group change now and add the account to the case.
card.if_clean: no privilege changes from this host.

evidence.title: Logons from this host (click a destination to follow)
evidence.expr: sum by (dst_host, user, logon_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | src_host="$host" | event_id="4624" | dst_host!="" | dst_host!="$host" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Allowed admin sessions from this host (click to follow)
evidence.expr: sum by (dst_host, dst_port, dst_zone, rule) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | src_host="$host" | dst_port=~"3389|445|5985" | action="allow" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Addresses scanned and denied
evidence.expr: count(sum by (dst_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | src_host="$host" | action="deny" | dst_zone!="internet" [$__range])))
evidence.help: Distinct internal addresses this host was blocked from. A high number is a scan for the next target.

card.look: machines this host logged on to or opened RDP, SMB or WinRM sessions to.
card.bad: RDP (3389), SMB (445) or WinRM (5985) to a server, jump host or plant system, especially into an `ot-*` zone.
card.if_bad: write this host down, then **click the destination** to make it the current hop. Start again at Step 1.
card.if_clean: nothing here means this is the end of the trail. Go to Step 5, then Decide.

steps.title: Did they cross into the plant network?

evidence.title: Controller events from this host (click to open WF5)
evidence.expr: sum by (site, asset, event_type, severity) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | src_host="$host" [$__range]))

card.look: plant controller events that came from this host.
card.bad: any controller change sourced from this host.
card.if_bad: click the asset to open WF5. Call the plant controls engineer before touching anything.
card.if_clean: nothing from this host reached a controller.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
You are done when Step 4 is empty on the last host. Your notes now hold the **host list** and the **account list**.

**Do these now:**
1. Contain every host on the list in EDR (plant systems: through the controls engineer, not EDR).
2. Disable or reset every account from Steps 1 to 3. Rotate passwords for each service account behind an RC4 ticket.
3. Revert group additions from Step 3 and remove installed services such as `PSEXESVC`.

**Then go to:**
- WF5 for any asset in Step 5 (click it)
- [[WF2 for the current hop]]
- [[Case timeline for the current hop]]

links.label: Case timeline for the current hop

rule.verdict: End of trail on this hop
rule.close_if_false: Step 4 found another hop. Follow it before deciding.

workflows.title: WF4 Data exfiltration
workflows.description: Size an outbound transfer, name the data, find where it came from, and confirm who sent it.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead D, or WF1/WF2 showed large uploads.  
**You need:** the user name.  
**Goal:** decide whether intellectual property left the company and how much. About 5 minutes.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

steps.title: How much left, and to where?

evidence.title: Total to file sharing
evidence.expr: sum(sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range]))

evidence.title: Upload volume by destination
evidence.expr: sum by (url_domain) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | method="POST" | unwrap bytes_out [$__interval]))

card.look: upload volume over time per destination.
card.bad: over 100 MB to a personal file-sharing or paste site, especially a run of near-identical chunks.
card.if_bad: block the destination at the proxy for everyone, then Step 2.
card.if_clean: uploads go to the corporate SharePoint or a sanctioned SaaS. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Uploaded files
evidence.expr: topk(50, sum by (url_domain, file_name) (sum_over_time({service_name="secdemo-proxy"} | json | user="$user" | category="file-sharing" | method="POST" | file_name!="" | unwrap bytes_out [$__range])))

card.look: file names on the uploads.
card.bad: archives split into numbered parts (`.7z.001`), program or vehicle platform names, CAD or battery data.
card.if_bad: send the file names to the data owner (engineering) to confirm sensitivity.
card.if_clean: personal files or nothing named. Check Step 3 before closing.

steps.title: Where did the files come from?

evidence.title: Shares opened by this user
evidence.expr: sum by (share, relative_target) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ad"} | json | user="$user" | event_id="5145" [$__range]))

card.look: file shares the user opened.
card.bad: an engineering share the user does not normally use, opened just before the uploads.
card.if_bad: the share owner needs to know. Add the share to the case.
card.if_clean: no share access. The data may have been local.

evidence.title: VPN sessions for this user
evidence.expr: sum by (event, src_ip, src_country, hip_compliant) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-vpn"} | json | user="$user" [$__range]))

card.look: how the user was connected while the uploads happened.
card.bad: VPN from abroad, a failed device posture check, or a sign-in workflow (WF1) that came back compromised.
card.if_bad: treat it as an attacker, not an insider. Run [[WF1 for this user]].
card.if_clean: on-site or normal VPN. Insider risk: involve HR and legal before contacting the user.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Confirmed exfiltration** if Step 1 was red and Step 2 or Step 3 names sensitive data.

**Do these now:**
1. Block the destination domain at the proxy for all users.
2. Notify the data owner with the file names and the total from Step 1.
3. If Step 4 says attacker: legal and privacy start the IP-theft process. If insider: HR and legal before anyone talks to the user.

**Then go to:**
- [[WF1 for this user]]
- [[Case timeline]]

also.say: Session was not the user. Treat as attacker, run WF1.

workflows.title: WF5 Plant floor change
workflows.description: Is an unticketed controller change an attack, is the process still safe, and how did they get there.
intro:
### Safety first
Do **not** isolate, reboot or push anything to a controller from the SOC. **Call the plant controls engineer on shift and the line supervisor before any action.** A controller in a bad state can hurt people. The SOC's job is to tell them what changed and from where.

**Use when:** Lead E, or WF3 Step 5 showed a controller event.  
**You need:** the plant and the asset.  
**Goal:** tell the plant team what changed, whether the process is safe, and who did it.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

evidence.title: Unticketed changes at this plant (click an asset)
evidence.expr: sum by (ot_line, asset, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | change_ticket="" | event_type=~"program_download|controller_mode_change|write_request" [$__range]))

card.look: every unticketed controller change at this plant.
card.bad: more than one asset changed in a short window.
card.if_bad: click the asset to work it. Do the busiest one first.
card.if_clean: if the asset you were sent here for is not listed, its change had a ticket. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Asset event log
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" | line_format "{{.severity}}  {{.event_type}}  {{.description}}  [{{.technique_id}}]  ticket={{.change_ticket}}" | keep service_name

card.look: every event on the asset, oldest first.
card.bad: RUN to PROGRAM mode change, program download, then PROGRAM back to RUN, with no change ticket. That is someone replacing logic.
card.if_bad: phone the controls engineer now with the asset name and the time. Then Step 2.
card.if_clean: a ticketed change inside the window. Close the lead.

evidence.title: Setpoint writes
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" | event_type="write_request" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Setpoint writes
evidence.expr: {service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" | event_type="write_request" | line_format "{{.description}}  by {{.user}} from {{.src_host}}" | keep service_name

card.look: setpoint writes on this asset.
card.bad: a setpoint pushed outside its engineering limits (oven, press force, torque, battery charge current).
card.if_bad: the controls engineer verifies the real value at the HMI and puts the line in a safe state. That is their call, not the SOC's.
card.if_clean: no setpoint writes. The logic change alone still needs review.

evidence.title: Source of the change (click the host)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, user, event_type) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | asset="$asset" [$__range]))

card.look: the workstation and account behind the change.
card.bad: an account that is not on the controls team, or an engineering workstation that also has EDR detections.
card.if_bad: click the host to open WF2 for it.
card.if_clean: the line's own engineer from their own workstation. Ask them whether they made the change.

steps.title: How did they reach the cell?

evidence.title: Connections into plant zones (click to open WF3)
evidence.expr: sum by (src_host, src_zone, dst_host, dst_zone, dst_port, rule) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | site="$site" | dst_zone=~"ot-.*" | action="allow" | src_host!~"HIST-.*" [$__range]))

card.look: who connected into the plant network zones at this site.
card.bad: a VPN address or office workstation going through the jump host, or anything into `ot-cell` that is not the historian.
card.if_bad: click the first host in the chain to open WF3 and walk it.
card.if_clean: only the historian and known engineering workstations.

evidence.title: New devices at this plant
evidence.expr: sum by (ot_line, asset, description) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-ot"} | json | site="$site" | event_type="new_asset" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Controller-port scans inside cells
evidence.expr: count by (src_host) (sum by (src_host, dst_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-firewall"} | json | site="$site" | src_zone="ot-cell" | action="deny" [$__range])))

card.look: new devices and scans inside the cells at this plant.
card.bad: an unknown device on a cell switch, or a workstation scanning controller ports (102 S7, 44818 EtherNet/IP, 502 Modbus).
card.if_bad: give the list to the controls engineer. Each one gets checked.
card.if_clean: no new devices and no scans.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Attack** if Step 1 shows an unticketed download or mode change **and** Step 3 or Step 4 is unexpected.

**Do these now (with the plant):**
1. Controls engineer restores the last known-good program and confirms setpoints.
2. Disable the account from Step 3 in the OT domain. Close the firewall rule from Step 4 that let the session in.
3. Preserve the controller project file and the workstation for forensics.

**Then go to:**
- WF2 for the workstation in Step 3 (click it)
- WF3 for the first host in Step 4 (click it)
- [[Case timeline for this asset]]

rule.close_if_false: Ticketed or explained change. Close the lead.

workflows.title: WF6 Vehicle API abuse
workflows.description: Partner or app key enumerating VINs or trying remote commands on customer cars.
intro:
**Use when:** Lead F.  
**You need:** the API key id.  
**Goal:** decide whether a key is being abused and whether any customer vehicle data was exposed.

Work the steps in order. Each card says what to look at, what bad looks like and where to go next. Blue values in tables open the next workflow with that value filled in.

steps.title: Is this key behaving differently from the others?

evidence.title: Error rate by key
evidence.expr: sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | status >= 400 [$__interval])) / sum by (api_key_id) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json [$__interval]))

card.look: error rate per key over time.
card.bad: one key's error rate far above the others (normal is about 2%).
card.if_bad: go to Step 2.
card.if_clean: this key looks like every other key. Close the lead.

steps.title: Where are the requests coming from?

evidence.title: Sources getting errors on this key
evidence.expr: topk(25, sum by (src_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | status >= 400 [$__range])))

evidence.title: All sources for this key, last 15 minutes
evidence.expr: sum by (src_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" [15m]))

card.look: source addresses for this key.
card.bad: an address outside the partner's registered egress range (`198.18.0.0/15` in this demo) sending most of the errors.
card.if_bad: that address is the abuser. Block it at the gateway and go to Step 3.
card.if_clean: all traffic is from the partner's range. Their system may be broken, not compromised. Call the partner.

evidence.title: Endpoints and outcomes
evidence.expr: sum by (method, endpoint, status) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" [$__range]))

evidence.title: Remote command attempts
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | endpoint=~".*/remote/.*" [$__range]))

card.look: endpoints and outcomes for this key.
card.bad: a wall of 404s on `/vehicles/{vin}/...` (guessing VINs), or any `/remote/` command (unlock, start).
card.if_bad: remote command attempts escalate to the vehicle security team right away.
card.if_clean: normal endpoints and status codes.

steps.title: Did they get any customer data?

evidence.title: Successful responses to unregistered addresses
evidence.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | status=200 | src_ip!~"198[.]18[.].*" [$__range]))

evidence.title: What was returned
evidence.expr: sum by (endpoint, src_ip) (count_over_time({service_name="secdemo-telematics"} | json | api_key_id="$api_key" | status=200 | src_ip!~"198[.]18[.].*" [$__range]))

card.look: successful responses to addresses outside the partner range.
card.bad: any 200. Each one is a real vehicle's status or location returned to the abuser.
card.if_bad: this is a privacy incident. Privacy and legal need the count and the time range.
card.if_clean: zero successes. Enumeration failed. Still revoke the key.

decide.markdown:
### Decide
**Abuse** if Step 1 is red and Step 2 shows an unregistered source.

**Do these now:**
1. Revoke the key and issue the partner a new one through their account manager.
2. Block the source address at the API gateway.
3. If Step 4 is above zero: open a privacy incident with the count of exposed vehicles.
4. If Step 3 shows remote commands: notify the vehicle security team.

**Then:** [[Case timeline for the source address]]

links.label: Case timeline for the source address

also.say: Customer vehicle data was returned. Open a privacy incident.

rule.close_if_false: Key behaves like the others. Close the lead.

workflows.title: Case timeline
workflows.description: Every source for one entity, in time order. Use it to write the case narrative.
intro: **How to use:** put one value in the Entity box (a user, host, IP, asset or file hash). Read the log **oldest first** and write one line per event in the case: time, source, what happened. Do this for every entity on your containment list. The first event across all of them is your initial access time.
